adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cycle guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` that only blocks outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., the same integration). From the code shown, this does not prevent a multi-integration bounce where Integration A’s inbound change triggers outbound to Integration B (allowed because ids differ), and B’s inbound could later trigger outbound back to A. The diff doesn’t show the full inbound webhook handlers or how differing assignees/races are handled, so the specific “ping-pong loop” scenario can’t be fully verified, but the limitation of the guard is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — Matching is by integration_id only, so an assignment arriving from external issue X suppresses outbound sync to every other linked external issue (Y, Z) in the same integration, leaving them silently out of sync.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` now suppresses outbound syncing whenever `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py). This check is only by integration id and does not consider which `ExternalIssue` triggered the inbound change, so if a group is linked to multiple `ExternalIssue`s under the same integration, an inbound assignment from one would prevent outbound sync for all links of that integration. However, the code comment indicates this broad suppression is intentional to prevent sync cycles, so it’s an edge-case/scope concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — Cycle guard is skipped entirely when from_dict fails (returns None on any TypeError/ValueError, e.g. schema drift during a rolling deploy with old/new workers), silently reverting to unguarded outbound sync with no log or metric.

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_assignee_outbound`, `assignment_source_dict` is parsed via `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)`, which returns `None` on `TypeError`/`ValueError`. The cycle guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)` only runs when `sync_source` is truthy (`if sync_source and ...: return False`). Therefore, if parsing fails, the guard is bypassed and outbound sync proceeds based solely on config. The diff shows no logging/metric on parse failure, so this fallback is silent. This is a real, diff-grounded edge case in the newly added cycle-prevention mechanism (though it does not clearly regress behavior vs. pre-change behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — assignment_source` was added to sync_status_outbound but no caller or inbound status path threads it, so status sync cycles remain unguarded despite the advertised feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `assignment_source`/`sync_source` concept and a cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)`, and threads it through the assignee outbound path (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> task -> `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). However, for status syncing, the only change shown is expanding the abstract `sync_status_outbound(..., assignment_source=None, **kwargs)` signature; there are no corresponding call-site or task changes in this diff that pass an `AssignmentSource` into `should_sync` for status attributes or into `sync_status_outbound`. So the finding that status cycle prevention is not demonstrably wired up by this PR is supported by what’s shown, but it’s an incompleteness/scope gap rather than a verifiable runtime defect introduced here.

The added tests only check `queued` is non-null and don’t exercise a `to_dict()` -> task kwargs -> `from_dict()` round-trip, so these issues would go undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31 — from_dict` round-trip does not restore `queued` to a datetime (stays a string after JSON transport) and silently returns None on any shape drift, disabling cycle prevention without logging.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` and `from_dict()` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` without parsing/coercing fields like `queued` back to a `datetime`. After task transport (e.g., JSON), `queued` could be a string and would remain so (dataclasses don’t enforce types), though the cycle-prevention logic added in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)` only relies on `integration_id`, not `queued`, so the “disabling cycle prevention” claim due to `queued` is not supported by the shown code. Separately, `from_dict()` does silently return `None` on `ValueError`/`TypeError` (no logging), and a malformed payload would bypass the new cycle-prevention check because `sync_source` becomes `None`, which is a real robustness/observability concern grounded in the diff but not a definite functional break in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, so the serialized `queued` field is a stale constant for every instance rather than the enqueue time.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. In Python, dataclass defaults are evaluated when the class is defined (module import time), so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp value. This makes `to_dict()` serialize a stale constant rather than the creation/enqueue time. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:382 — should_sync` takes the new param as `sync_source` while every other boundary names it `assignment_source`, making the positional/keyword contract inconsistent for overriders.

adjudication.rationale: In `issues.py`, `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` introduce the new optional parameter named `sync_source`, while the rest of the diff consistently uses `assignment_source` for the same concept (e.g., `sync_status_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`, `sync_group_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`, `GroupAssignee.assign/deassign(..., assignment_source=...)`, and the task kwarg `assignment_source_dict`). This isn’t a proven runtime bug in this diff because current calls pass the value positionally (`installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`), but it does create an inconsistent keyword/override contract: any keyword call using `assignment_source=` would fail for `should_sync` unless renamed/aligned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:30 — to_dict puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs, which a JSON serializer can't handle, and from_dict doesn't convert it back, so `queued` comes back as a string or the enqueue fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` the dataclass is converted via `asdict(self)`, which will include `queued` as a `datetime` object (not an ISO string). That dict is then passed into Celery task kwargs as `assignment_source_dict` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` (`apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})`). If the task queue uses a JSON-based serializer (common/default), a raw `datetime` is not JSON-serializable and enqueueing will fail. Additionally, `from_dict()` just does `cls(**input_dict)` and does not parse/convert `queued`, so even if serialization coerces it to a string, it would come back as a string rather than a `datetime`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:33 — from_dict drops unknown keys only by failing: any extra or renamed key (for example, a newer payload shape) raises TypeError and returns None, which quietly turns off cycle prevention and brings back the sync loop.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict` the implementation `return cls(**input_dict)` will raise `TypeError` if `input_dict` contains any unknown keys, and the method then returns `None` (lines added in `assignment_source.py`). That behavior is real and means the cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` is skipped when parsing fails. However, in this diff the only producer of `assignment_source_dict` is `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (via `sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> task kwargs), which uses `asdict(self)` and therefore matches the expected fields, so no concrete failure is shown here. The concern is forward/backward compatibility (e.g., a newer payload adding keys during a rolling deploy) rather than an immediately verifiable defect in the current diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:389 — The cycle check only covers outbound assignee sync; the new assignment_source parameter on sync_status_outbound is never passed or checked, so status sync cycles still happen.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that only takes effect when callers pass a non-None `sync_source`. In this PR, the only shown call site updated to pass/parse an `AssignmentSource` is outbound assignee sync (`sync_assignee_outbound` task calling `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and then passing `assignment_source` into `sync_assignee_outbound`). Although `sync_status_outbound`’s signature is extended to accept `assignment_source`, no status-sync call sites are shown being updated to pass it or to call `should_sync` with it, so the cycle-prevention mechanism is not demonstrably applied to status sync in this diff. However, the claim that status sync cycles “still happen” is not directly verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:34 — New `assignment_source_dict` task kwarg is sent by producers before all workers are upgraded, so old workers raise TypeError during a rolling deploy and the non-excluded error burns through 5 retries, dropping the sync.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task signature `sync_assignee_outbound(...)` to accept a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict` (with default `None`) and updates the producer in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` to always enqueue that kwarg in `apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": ...})`. During a rolling deploy, any worker still running the old task signature (without this kwarg) would receive a message containing an unexpected keyword argument and raise `TypeError`, causing retries/failures and potentially dropping the sync. This incompatibility is directly implied by the producer now sending the new kwarg.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141 — to_dict()` puts a raw `datetime` into the celery kwargs, which a JSON task serializer can't reliably encode or decode back to a datetime; send an ISO string or epoch instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` the dataclass is converted via `asdict(self)`, which will include `queued` as a raw `datetime` object. In `sync_group_assignee_outbound` this dict is passed directly into Celery task kwargs as `assignment_source_dict` (`sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})`). If the task serializer is JSON (common for Celery), raw `datetime` values are not JSON-serializable and can cause scheduling/execution failures or lossy encoding/decoding. The diff clearly shows a `datetime` is being put into Celery kwargs without conversion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource gets the same stale process-start timestamp; use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

This calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so all `AssignmentSource` instances that don't pass `queued` will share the same timestamp value. For per-instance timestamps it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — Cycle suppression only checks the immediate source integration, so an A->Sentry->B->Sentry->A ping-pong between two linked integrations can still loop indefinitely.

It does not track/propagate a chain of sources beyond the immediate one (`AssignmentSource` only stores a single `integration_id`), so a cross-integration ping-pong (A inbound -> Sentry -> B outbound, then B inbound -> Sentry -> A outbound) is not prevented by the new logic. This is a real, diff-grounded limitation/edge case of the newly added suppression, but whether it “loops indefinitely” depends on behavior outside the shown diff.
